registry.description: The shared registry is global 0x95df4c. Records are linked with next+0, previous+4, a 32-byte name at +8, and a float value at +0x28. Registry free-list head/tail are +8/+12 and active-list head/tail +16/+20. A non-null cached third argument is returned directly when the registry is non-null. Lookup adds msg_ unless a case-insensitive occurrence of msg_ appears anywhere in the supplied name. Unprefixed names longer than 26 bytes are rejected. Active records are scanned in order, case-insensitively, before transferring the first free record to the active tail. Transfer does not zero the record value. Exhaustion returns null.
registry.qualification: Native disassembly establishes the returned cached-pointer path, which Ghidra typed void. Original literal at 0x805d48 is msg_. The already-prefixed sprintf branch lacks a name-length check; fixtures exclude its overflow domain, and the portable API rejects >31 characters.

Message.description: The condition initializer resolves/creates its name in the shared registry when its first argument, name pointer and global registry are nonzero. The condition reads the current float at its bound record+0x28, or zero for a null record. It reads the live value each evaluation. It does not dequeue notifications or use the packet blocked-message mask.

SetMessage.description: Always completes (returns 1). Only first-call, non-null-registry, positive-argument-count calls scan arguments. Each argument is searched case-insensitively, in name=, value=, increment=, decrement= priority. Matches can begin inside a longer token. Last matching name and numeric amount win; increment/decrement set mode +1/-1, while value= does not reset an earlier mode. Default amount and mode are zero. A valid name lookup is set, incremented or decremented as a float32 value. Failed lookup is ignored.

SetAIMessage.description: GIT updates the same shared registry. It searches Name and Val without the equals sign, then skips the key plus one separator byte. Increment/decrement use their equals-suffixed keys. Token order and persistent operation mode match SetMessage. Numeric operands use the decimal-prefix parser directly, without SCP packet parameter lookup. This handler has no first-call guard and no failed-lookup guard.

CopyMessage.description: On first call with a non-null registry and positive argument count, scan from= before to= inside each token; last matched source/destination names win. Resolve/create source first, then destination even if source lookup failed. If both resolve, copy all 32 value bits. Negative zero and quiet-NaN payload fixtures confirm a bit copy. Newly created source records retain their free-list values. The action always returns 1.

operands.description: SCP numeric operands first search the entire token for param, case-insensitively. The PC passes the beginning of that match to its integer parser, so param0, param3 and prefixPaRaM99 all resolve to packet parameter 0. Without such a match, ordered case-insensitive script parameter names map to the four packet values. Otherwise parse an optional minus and decimal digits/dot, stopping at the first other character; leading plus, whitespace and exponent notation are not accepted. Digit multiplication, digit addition, decimal divisor multiplication and final division store float32 values.
operands.qualification: The slot-zero result is confirmed by 40 direct operand fixtures here and independently by the root combat-command fixture. No general expression evaluator is implied.

puzzleLink.description: For all 34 authored GIT SetAIMessage occurrences, isolated original-PC tests construct a bound Message condition, perform the graph command, then call the original SCP scheduler 0x52cc90. The expected state is entered after the shared value update. This proves the command-to-record-to-condition-to-state contract on the controlled fixtures, not the reachability of those graph nodes or whole-level completion.

adapters.scope: Only %s or %s%s, ASCII fixtures and bounded output <32 bytes. Does not model CRT locale, allocator or OS imports.

portable.status: Core library and message comparison harness compiled with installed C# 5 compiler. Execution/differential comparison pending; root reports Windows denial of newly generated managed executables.
adapters: Host constructs registry capacity and initial free-record value bits and owns its lifetime. No recovered level-load/reset policy is invented.
Host binds ScriptDefinition.ParameterNames and packet values from source loader.
SCP condition comparisons and graph activation remain separate scheduler integrations; native bounded chain fixtures verify the connection.
hostGuards: Reject embedded NUL/non-ASCII text rather than approximate native extended-byte case folding.
Reject already-prefixed names longer than 31 characters rather than reproduce stack overflow.
Throw on GIT missing registry/name/capacity instead of native failed-lookup dereference.

remaining: ASCII names only; embedded NUL and overlong names already containing msg_ are excluded because original sprintf lacks a bound on that branch.
GIT SetAIMessage requires a valid registry, name and available record. Original handler dereferences a failed lookup; portable source will explicitly reject that invalid input.
Registry lifecycle/allocation/reset and inter-level message persistence are not established by these isolated fixtures.
Native reference fixtures are not a compiled C# differential pass.
